hook: Greenland and Antarctica ice loss explains 51% of the speedup in global sea level rise since 1993.

readout.label: Share of sea level acceleration from ice sheets

summary: Sea level rise has sped up over three decades, and the ice sheets' share was unclear. The authors extended satellite gravity records of ice mass back to 1993 and found both ice sheets are losing mass at an increasing rate. With mountain glaciers, land ice still leaves part of the acceleration unexplained.
title: Greenland and Antarctica Dominate Recent Acceleration in Global Mean Sea Level Rise: 1993–2023
